title: Fire destroys Chad le Clos's home after Commonwealth record
seoTitle: Fire destroys Chad le Clos home after Commonwealth record
subtitle: South African swimmer celebrates Commonwealth Games feat before losing his home
excerpt: On August 4, 2026, Chad le Clos revealed that a fire destroyed his apartment in Sea Point after breaking the Commonwealth Games medal record.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On August 4, 2026, South African swimmer Chad le Clos announced that a fire devastated his apartment in Sea Point, Cape Town, a few days after setting the historic medal record at the Commonwealth Games. The athlete, who already has 21 medals from the competition, mourned the loss of his home and a neighbor who died in the tragedy.

Historic record at the Commonwealth Games

Le Clos earned his 21st medal by surpassing Australian Emma McKeon, becoming the athlete with the most medals in Commonwealth Games history. At the 2026 edition, he won bronze in the men's 4x100 m medley relay, silver in the mixed 4x100 m medley relay, and bronze in the men's 4x100 m freestyle relay, completing his third podium finish at the competition. He began collecting Commonwealth medals in Delhi 2010 at age 18, and today totals seven golds, five silvers and nine bronzes across five editions.

Fire destroys apartment in Sea Point

On the night of July 30, a fire broke out in the apartment block where le Clos lives and quickly spread to his home, which he had occupied for more than a decade. According to the swimmer’s own statement, “nothing left to salvage” – nothing was left to be saved – and the property was consumed by the flames.

Tribute to the deceased neighbor

In a message posted on Instagram, le Clos wrote: “It has taken me a while to process this heartbreaking tragedy”. He also noted that the fire occurred “amid breaking the all-time Commonwealth record”. The athlete expressed his condolences to the victim’s family, stating that “no words can truly ease a loss like this, but I hope the family knows that the thoughts of an entire community are with them”.

Fundraising campaign for the neighbors

To help the affected residents, le Clos launched a fundraising campaign, seeking resources to help rebuild homes and support the families impacted by the tragedy.

Le Clos's sporting legacy

Throughout his career, the South African swimmer has collected four Olympic medals, 16 world titles, seven Commonwealth golds and 10 African titles. He became famous for defeating Michael Phelps in the 200 m butterfly at the London 2012 Olympics, and remains one of the leading figures in international swimming.

With information from BBC Sport.
